sentences.text: Utahceratops was a large, robust quadrupedal herbivore that could grow to an estimated length of 4.5 to 5 meters.
Scientists estimate this animal weighed approximately 2 tonnes.
It possessed short, robust supraorbital horncores that were blunt-tipped and directed dorsolaterally.
The lateral frill featured extremely elongate episquamosals, some measuring over 10 centimeters in length.
Six specimens are known, preserving about 96% of the skull and 70% of the postcranial skeleton.
The specific name gettyi honors Mike Getty, who discovered the holotype and aided in fossil recovery.
The genus Utahceratops was first named by Scott D. Sampson and six other researchers in 2010.
The name Utahceratops means "horned face from Utah", derived from the state name and Greek words for horn and face.

Utahceratops shared its environment with diverse dinosaurs including dromaeosaurids, tyrannosaurids like Teratophoneus, ankylosaurids, hadrosaurs like Parasaurolophus and Gryposaurus, and other ceratopsians.
The paleofauna of the Kaiparowits Formation included chondrichthyans, amphibians, turtles, lizards, and crocodilians.
Primitive mammals, including multituberculates, marsupials, and insectivorans, were present in the Kaiparowits Formation.
Utahceratops is classified as a basal chasmosaurine ceratopsian.
It is found in a clade of basal chasmosaurines that includes Pentaceratops.
Utahceratops lived approximately 76.4 to 75.5 million years ago in what is now Utah.
The habitat was an ancient floodplain dominated by channels, wetland peat swamps, ponds, and lakes, bordered by highlands.
It is debated whether Albertosaurus and Ornithomimus velox were present in the Kaiparowits Formation, as existing fossil evidence is not conclusive.
